app.name: HubSpot
app.one_liner: Straightforward OAuth, but new apps use Projects/CLI and Marketplace listing adds real review work.

headline: HubSpot OAuth is not hard for a normal CRM integration: you can create and test a Projects-based OAuth app with a free HubSpot account, usually in about an hour. The main gate is not basic OAuth production use; it is optional Marketplace listing, and sensitive-data scopes add partner/review requirements that can stretch launch by weeks.

production_review.detail: For ordinary OAuth scopes, HubSpot does not require Marketplace approval before an unlisted app can be installed, although users may see unverified/unreviewed warnings. Review becomes a real gate if you want Marketplace listing, and sensitive-data scopes require an approval process with HubSpot Ecosystem Quality before production allowlisting.

review_wait.detail: Normal unlisted OAuth use has no provider review wait. Marketplace submissions get an initial review within 10 business days, and HubSpot says the review/feedback process should take no more than 60 days from feedback; sensitive-data review timing is not published separately.

security_assessment.detail: HubSpot does not publish a universal third-party security audit requirement for every OAuth app. For sensitive-data scopes, Ecosystem Quality may evaluate the organization’s overall security posture during the approval process.

business_verification.detail: A paid account or formal legal-entity verification is not required to develop OAuth apps. Marketplace listing does require live Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, support, setup documentation, pricing, and data-disclosure materials, but the provided docs do not describe this as legal-entity verification.

gated_access.detail: You can create apps with a free HubSpot account, developer test accounts, and API access for development/testing. Production users need appropriate HubSpot accounts, and some APIs depend on the customer’s HubSpot product tier.

dev_mode_limits.detail: Projects-based apps can be configured for Marketplace distribution or restricted installation to specific HubSpot accounts. Unverified/unlisted apps can be installed, but HubSpot shows risk/review warning banners; the researched docs do not publish a universal external-user cap for unlisted Projects apps.

customer_admin_approval.detail: The installer must have access to the app’s required or conditionally required scopes and the required HubSpot user permissions. In many customer portals, that means an admin or a user with app-install permissions must perform or approve the connection.

effort.explanation: A basic unlisted OAuth app is mostly CLI setup, redirect URI configuration, token exchange, and CRM API testing, so a competent developer can get a first install in about 45–90 minutes and a production-ready integration in 1–3 days. The upper end assumes Marketplace listing or sensitive-data access: you need public docs, privacy/legal/support pages, install evidence from at least three unaffiliated production accounts for listing, scope justifications, and back-and-forth with HubSpot review.

start_here.action: Create a Projects-based HubSpot app with the HubSpot CLI and choose OAuth when prompted.
start_here.why: New legacy public-app creation has been disabled; new public OAuth apps should be built on HubSpot’s Projects-based platform.

phases.name: Prepare
phases.goal: Decide whether you need only unlisted OAuth installs, Marketplace listing, or sensitive-data access before you build the app shape.

steps.title: Create or choose a HubSpot developer account
steps.detail: Use a free HubSpot account if you do not already have one; HubSpot states paid HubSpot is not required to create apps and test API access.

steps.title: Decide the distribution path
steps.detail: Choose Marketplace distribution if you want HubSpot Marketplace listing and removal of review/unverified warning banners. Choose restricted installation if you only want installation in specific HubSpot accounts during development or private rollout.

steps.title: Inventory the minimum HubSpot data your agent needs
steps.detail: List every CRM object and action the AI agent will perform, then map each to least-privilege scopes such as `crm.objects.contacts.read` or `crm.objects.contacts.write`. HubSpot requires apps to request only needed scopes and actually use all requested scopes for Marketplace listing.

steps.title: Avoid sensitive-data scopes unless you truly need them
steps.detail: If your agent needs sensitive data scopes, plan for HubSpot technology partner eligibility, Ecosystem Quality approval, possible security-posture evaluation, development/staging allowlisting, production allowlisting, and customer re-authorization.

phases.name: Register the app
phases.goal: Create the Projects-based OAuth app and obtain app credentials.

steps.title: Install and authenticate the HubSpot CLI
steps.detail: Install the HubSpot CLI, then run `hs account auth` and authenticate it to the HubSpot account that will own the app. HubSpot’s app-creation docs recommend CLI v7.6.0 or newer on that page.

steps.title: Create a new project app
steps.detail: Run `hs project create`. During the prompts, select the app distribution model and choose OAuth for authenticating multiple HubSpot accounts; static-token auth is for apps limited to a specific account.

steps.title: Use Projects, not legacy public-app creation
steps.detail: Do not plan around creating a new legacy public app in the UI. HubSpot disabled new legacy public-app creation in 2026; existing legacy apps continue to function, but new public app development should use Projects-based apps.

steps.title: Record the OAuth client values
steps.detail: Capture the HubSpot app ID, OAuth client ID, and OAuth client secret from the developer app configuration. Store the client secret only in your server-side secret store; HubSpot token exchange requires `client_secret`.

phases.name: Configure OAuth
phases.goal: Make the install URL, redirect handler, token exchange, and refresh flow work safely.

steps.title: Add your redirect URI
steps.detail: Configure the exact HTTPS redirect URI your app will use, for example `https://app.example.com/oauth/hubspot/callback`. The same `redirect_uri` must be sent in the authorization request and authorization-code token exchange.

steps.title: Build the authorization URL
steps.detail: Use `https://app.hubspot.com/oauth/authorize` with `client_id`, space-delimited `scope`, `redirect_uri`, and `state`. If you have optional scopes, send them with HubSpot’s optional scope query parameter rather than making them required.

steps.title: Implement the authorization-code exchange
steps.detail: POST `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` to `https://api.hubspot.com/oauth/v3/token` with `grant_type=authorization_code`, `code`, `redirect_uri`, `client_id`, and `client_secret`. Store the returned access token expiry and refresh token.

steps.title: Implement refresh-token rotation handling
steps.detail: Refresh with a form-encoded POST to the same v3 token endpoint using `grant_type=refresh_token`, `refresh_token`, `client_id`, and `client_secret`. HubSpot access tokens expire after 30 minutes; design your agent runtime to refresh before API calls fail.

steps.title: Include PKCE if your OAuth library supports it
steps.detail: HubSpot’s public docs found in this pass do not state public-app PKCE requirements, but its OAuth metadata advertises `S256` code challenge support. Treat PKCE as supported and verify behavior with your actual app registration before depending on it as mandatory.

phases.name: Test with your own account
phases.goal: Prove that a real HubSpot user can install the app and your agent can call HubSpot APIs with OAuth.

steps.title: Open the install URL in a HubSpot account
steps.detail: Sign in as a HubSpot user who has access to the app’s required scopes and install permissions. The install flow prompts the user to review app permissions.

steps.title: Acknowledge unverified-app warnings during private testing
steps.detail: If the app is unlisted or unverified, HubSpot may show warnings and require the user to type `I accept the risk` before connecting. This is expected for unreviewed/unlisted apps and is different from Marketplace approval.

steps.title: Exchange the callback code and call a scoped API
steps.detail: After redirect, exchange the `code` for tokens and immediately call one API covered by each required scope, such as reading or writing contacts for `crm.objects.contacts.read` / `crm.objects.contacts.write`. This also produces app activity useful for Marketplace eligibility.

steps.title: Verify token metadata if debugging
steps.detail: Use HubSpot’s `/oauth/v3/token/introspect` endpoint to inspect access-token or refresh-token metadata when you need to confirm token state during development.

phases.name: Get Marketplace approval or sensitive-scope approval if needed
phases.goal: Complete only the provider approvals that match your distribution and data requirements.

steps.title: Skip Marketplace submission if you only need direct/private installs
steps.detail: Marketplace listing is for distribution, discoverability, and removal of warning banners. Do not count it as a required OAuth production gate if your customers can install directly and can tolerate the unreviewed-app warning.

steps.title: Collect three unaffiliated active production installs before listing
steps.detail: For Marketplace listing, HubSpot requires at least three active, unique installs in unaffiliated HubSpot production accounts, with app activity in the past 30 days. App activity includes OAuth-authenticated HubSpot API requests and signed requests from HubSpot webhooks or extensions.

steps.title: Prepare the Marketplace listing package
steps.detail: Create live Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs, public setup documentation, support resources, support contact, accurate pricing, accurate shared-data disclosures, screenshots that match the app, and scope justifications. The app must use OAuth as its sole authorization method for the listing.

steps.title: Submit only one app for approval at a time
steps.detail: HubSpot automatically rejects additional apps submitted while another app is in active review. Sequence submissions if your company has multiple HubSpot apps.

steps.title: Wait for HubSpot review and respond to feedback
steps.detail: HubSpot’s Ecosystem Quality team manually reviews Marketplace submissions. Expect an initial response within 10 business days and plan for back-and-forth on scopes, data disclosures, setup docs, pricing, screenshots, and app behavior.

phases.name: Launch and maintain
phases.goal: Run OAuth reliably for real customers and keep the app compliant with HubSpot’s platform changes.

steps.title: Handle customer permission failures in onboarding
steps.detail: Tell customers that the installing user must have access to all required or conditionally required scopes. Provide an admin handoff path when a non-admin user cannot install.

steps.title: Monitor refresh failures and app activity
steps.detail: Track token refresh errors, install/uninstall events, and successful OAuth-authenticated API requests. Marketplace eligibility and continued listing quality depend on real app activity and correct OAuth use.

steps.title: Stay current with HubSpot platform versions
steps.detail: HubSpot’s Developer Platform uses March/September date-based versions, each supported for 18 months. Schedule maintenance so your project does not drift onto unsupported patterns.

steps.title: Do not build new classic CRM cards
steps.detail: If your app uses HubSpot UI surfaces, avoid classic CRM cards; HubSpot listing requirements say classic CRM cards are no longer supported as of June 16, 2025.

requirements.detail: A paid HubSpot account is not required to create and test apps; production users need appropriate HubSpot accounts and product tiers for the APIs they use.
New Projects-based apps are initialized with the HubSpot CLI. Authenticate with `hs account auth`, then create the project with `hs project create`.
You need an exact redirect URI and must reuse the same value in the authorization URL and token exchange.
HubSpot policy and Marketplace listing requirements say apps must request only scopes they need and use all scopes requested during installation.

requirements.item: Public Terms, Privacy Policy, setup docs, support, pricing, and data disclosures
requirements.detail: Required for HubSpot Marketplace listing submissions; not established by the provided docs as a prerequisite for direct unlisted OAuth installs.
Marketplace listing requires at least three active, unique installs in unaffiliated production accounts with app activity in the past 30 days.
Sensitive-data scopes are available only to HubSpot technology partners with at least one public Marketplace app and require Ecosystem Quality approval and production allowlisting.

requirements.item: Optional domain verification for unlisted legacy public apps
requirements.detail: For non-Marketplace-listed legacy public apps, verifying a company domain with a DNS TXT record can reduce install-page warnings, but Marketplace-listed apps do not need domain verification.

scopes.purpose: Read HubSpot contact records so the AI agent can answer questions or sync CRM context.
Create or update HubSpot contact records when the user asks the agent to write CRM changes.
OAuth query parameter for scopes that improve functionality but should not block installation if the customer cannot grant them.
Access HubSpot-defined sensitive data. Use only if the agent truly requires this data because it triggers partner/listing and approval constraints.

gotchas.title: New public apps are Projects-based, not legacy UI public apps
gotchas.detail: HubSpot disabled new legacy public-app creation in 2026. Existing legacy apps continue working, but new public OAuth app development should use the Projects-based app platform and CLI.

gotchas.title: Marketplace listing is not the same as OAuth being usable
gotchas.detail: Unlisted/unverified apps can be installed, but users see risk and unreviewed-app warnings. Marketplace review is required for listing/discoverability and warning removal, not for every direct OAuth install path.

gotchas.title: Marketplace listing has a chicken-and-egg install requirement
gotchas.detail: HubSpot requires three active, unique, unaffiliated production installs before listing submission. Community reports suggest this first-three-installs requirement is a practical hurdle for new apps.

gotchas.title: Sensitive-data scopes are a separate, stricter path
gotchas.detail: Sensitive-data access requires partner eligibility, at least one public Marketplace app, an approval request, review, development/staging allowlisting, compliance verification, production allowlisting, and customer re-authorization.

gotchas.title: AI connector Marketplace rules may affect architecture
gotchas.detail: HubSpot says AI connectors primarily connecting HubSpot to external generative AI tools must use user-level permissions or be built with HubSpot’s MCP Server to qualify for Marketplace listing.

gotchas.title: Scope overreach causes review problems
gotchas.detail: Marketplace requirements and HubSpot’s Developer Policy require least-privilege scopes. Anecdotal reports say rejections often focus on data-handling disclosures, OAuth scope justification, and UI/listing mismatch.

gotchas.title: HubSpot API hostnames differ across docs and metadata
gotchas.detail: The v3 token docs use `https://api.hubspot.com/oauth/v3/token`; the discovered OAuth metadata returned a token endpoint on `api.hubapi.com` for v1. Use the v3 endpoint from HubSpot’s token-management docs for new OAuth token exchange unless HubSpot support tells you otherwise.

blockers.symptom: You cannot find the old “Create public app” UI flow
blockers.likely_cause: New legacy public-app creation was sunset in 2026.
blockers.what_to_do: Install the HubSpot CLI, authenticate with `hs account auth`, and create a Projects-based app with `hs project create`.

blockers.symptom: Install page shows an unverified or unreviewed app warning and asks the user to type `I accept the risk`
blockers.likely_cause: The app is unlisted or not Marketplace-reviewed, and possibly domain-unverified.
blockers.what_to_do: For private/direct rollout, document the warning in customer onboarding. To remove Marketplace review warning banners, complete Marketplace listing review; for legacy unlisted apps, domain verification may reduce some warnings.

blockers.symptom: A customer user cannot install the app
blockers.likely_cause: The user lacks access to the app’s required or conditionally required scopes, or lacks the required app-install permissions in that HubSpot portal.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask a HubSpot admin or a user with the required permissions to install, or reduce required scopes and move nonessential scopes to optional scopes.

blockers.symptom: Marketplace submission is rejected because the app lacks enough installs
blockers.likely_cause: HubSpot requires at least three active, unique installs in unaffiliated production accounts with recent app activity before listing.
blockers.what_to_do: Run a private beta with three unaffiliated production customers, ensure OAuth-authenticated API calls occur within 30 days, then resubmit.

blockers.symptom: Additional app submissions are automatically rejected
blockers.likely_cause: HubSpot allows only one app to be submitted for approval at a time.
blockers.what_to_do: Wait until the active review finishes before submitting another app.

blockers.likely_cause: The authorization code is missing, fake, expired, already used, or does not match the redirect URI/client credentials.
blockers.what_to_do: Generate a fresh install URL, complete the authorization flow again, and POST the exact `code`, `redirect_uri`, `client_id`, and `client_secret` to the v3 token endpoint as form-encoded data.

blockers.symptom: Sensitive-data scopes are unavailable or not approved for production
blockers.likely_cause: Sensitive data scopes require HubSpot technology partner status, a Marketplace app prerequisite, Ecosystem Quality approval, and production allowlisting.
blockers.what_to_do: Remove the sensitive scopes if possible. If unavoidable, start the sensitive-data approval process and plan for customer re-authorization after production allowlisting.

agent_can: Draft the least-privilege HubSpot scope list and one-line justification for each scope.
Generate the authorization URL template, `.env` template, token-exchange code, refresh-token job, and token introspection/debug script.
Check redirect URI consistency between app config, authorization URL, and token exchange code.
Draft Marketplace listing materials: setup guide, support text, scope explanations, shared-data disclosures, and review-response answers.
Create a customer onboarding checklist that explains HubSpot permissions, app owner behavior, and unverified-app warnings.
Monitor HubSpot changelogs for platform-version, user-level app, and listing-requirement changes.
you_must: Sign in to HubSpot and authenticate the CLI, because account access and terms acceptance require a human-controlled HubSpot account.
Choose the owning HubSpot account, app distribution model, and whether Marketplace listing is worth the review burden.
Copy/store the real client secret in your secret manager; an agent should never receive or print production secrets unnecessarily.
Perform any DNS TXT record changes for domain verification, because this requires control of your company domain.
Submit Marketplace or sensitive-data approval forms and respond to legal/compliance questions, because they bind your company and may require business judgment.
Recruit or coordinate the three unaffiliated production installs required for Marketplace listing.

artifacts.title: HubSpot OAuth environment template
artifacts.note: Keep `HUBSPOT_CLIENT_SECRET` server-side only. Add only the scopes your agent actually uses.

artifacts.title: Review-ready scope justification starter
artifacts.content:
crm.objects.contacts.read — Required to read contact records so the AI agent can answer user questions and synchronize CRM context.
crm.objects.contacts.write — Required only if the AI agent can create or update contact records at the user’s request.
optional_scope=<scope> — Use for nonessential capabilities so customers can install the core app even when they cannot grant the extra permission.

Data minimization statement: The app requests only the HubSpot scopes needed for the enabled agent actions and exercises each requested scope during normal operation.
artifacts.note: Adapt this to your exact CRM objects and remove write scopes if your agent is read-only.

artifacts.title: Example HubSpot authorization URL
artifacts.note: Add optional scopes using HubSpot’s optional-scope query parameter if needed. Keep `state` signed and single-use.

artifacts.title: Token exchange request shape
artifacts.content:
POST https://api.hubspot.com/oauth/v3/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=authorization_code&code=<AUTHORIZATION_CODE>&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.example.com%2Foauth%2Fhubspot%2Fcallback&client_id=<CLIENT_ID>&client_secret=<CLIENT_SECRET>

Refresh:
POST https://api.hubspot.com/oauth/v3/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=<REFRESH_TOKEN>&client_id=<CLIENT_ID>&client_secret=<CLIENT_SECRET>
artifacts.note: HubSpot access tokens expire after 30 minutes; persist refresh tokens securely.

oauth.refresh_tokens: HubSpot returns a long-term refresh token with the access token after OAuth installation; refresh by POSTing `grant_type=refresh_token`, `refresh_token`, `client_id`, and `client_secret` to the v3 token endpoint.
oauth.access_token_lifetime: 30 minutes; token responses include `expires_in`, with examples showing 1800 seconds.

uncertainties: HubSpot public docs found in this pass do not clearly state whether PKCE is mandatory, optional, or unsupported for each Projects-based public-app type. The OAuth metadata advertises S256, so test PKCE with your real app and confirm with HubSpot support if this is a compliance requirement.

The researched docs do not publish a universal external-user cap for unlisted Projects-based public apps beyond restricted-account distribution and Marketplace-listing requirements. Confirm your selected distribution mode in the developer portal before launch.

HubSpot does not publish a universal security-assessment checklist for all Marketplace apps in these sources. If you request sensitive-data scopes or AI-connector listing, ask HubSpot Ecosystem Quality what evidence they need before you submit.
Exact customer-side permission names for installing apps can vary by HubSpot account configuration. Validate the installer role and permissions in at least one target customer portal during beta.

score.label: Hard
score.blurb: Formal review, verification or gated access; plan weeks.

open_questions: HubSpot's current public docs found in this pass do not specify PKCE support or requirements for public-app OAuth; verify with HubSpot if PKCE is mandatory, optional, or unsupported for your app type.

HubSpot docs found here do not publish a general external-user cap for unlisted Projects-based public apps beyond allowlisted-account distribution and Marketplace requirements; confirm if your distribution model has install limits before launch.

HubSpot's docs do not publish a universal security-assessment checklist for all Marketplace apps beyond listing requirements and the sensitive-data review process; security posture review may vary by requested features/scopes.
Exact customer-side permission names for installing apps can vary by HubSpot account configuration; validate the required installer permissions in a target customer portal before rollout.

probes.summary: Endpoint is live and handles an unregistered client: HTTP 200 (mentions "client_id").
Token endpoint is live and rejects fake credentials: HTTP 400 "invalid_request".
